targetTest: An empty plugin reference is rejected as an empty plugin name - #1.8
expected: One usage-error payload per command with the verb's own usage line, kind usage-error, severity error, and needs reload false: Plugin name must not be empty. for update '', fetch '', and reinstall '', and Marketplace name must not be empty. for update @, fetch @, reinstall @, and reinstall '@   '.
actual: update '', fetch '', and reinstall '' report Invalid <plugin>@<marketplace> ref: "". and update @, fetch @, and reinstall @ report Invalid <plugin>@<marketplace> ref: "@"., each with the right kind, severity, and usage; reinstall '@   ' is not rejected at all and reaches the reinstall workflow, which returns a marketplace-not-added payload for a marketplace named "   ".
semanticAssessment: Fourteen scenarios ran: rows #1.1 to #1.7 of the empty-reference Outline (uninstall, enable, disable, install, info) passed, and the seven new targets failed only at the result has these fields step, after Pi started and ran the command. Rows #1.8 (update ''), #1.9 (fetch ''), and #1.10 (reinstall '') differ on the message row alone: the handlers split the reference with no empty check and report the invalid-reference message for "". Rows #1.1 (update @), #1.2 (fetch @), and #1.3 (reinstall @) of the new Outline differ on the message row alone: a bare @ fails the marketplace-form length check and falls through to the reference split. Row #1.4 (reinstall '@   ') differs on kind, message, and usage because the handler takes it as the marketplace form with a blank name and the reinstall workflow reports a marketplace named "   " as not added. Every failure is the planned assertion for the intended reason; there is no setup, load, or unrelated failure.
